title: Length Tessellator: Entropy-driven Bucketing and Pad-shearing for Micro-batch Packing
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Padding overhead in production workloads is a dominant contributor to per-token cost. Incoming request length distribution is multimodal across customers and routes; naive fixed bucketing or single pass coalescing wastes GPU cycles and increases latency variance. We need a runtime component that shapes micro-batches to minimize pad tokens while preserving latency SLOs and kernel efficiency.

Goal: Implement a length tessellation pipeline ("Tessellator") that: (1) constructs lightweight entropy-aware buckets at request ingress, (2) emits kernel-selection hints for each bucket to pick optimal fused or unfused attention kernels, (3) performs pad-shearing to remove contiguous suffix padding and enable compact KV layouts, and (4) integrates with prefill/decode schedulers to prioritize prefill coalescing across similar prefixes. The end goal is 10-30% reduction in padded tokens on representative traffic with <=5% tail-latency regression and no model-level correctness impact.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime produces buckets with average intra-bucket length variance < 12 tokens on sampled production traffic
Token-padding reduced by >= 10% on median routes and >= 20% on top-10 routes in staging A/B
No increase in top-99 latency > 5% compared to baseline when tessellator is enabled under identical load
Kernel selection hints lead to >=8% throughput improvement for affected buckets in microbenchmarks
End-to-end QA shows no semantic regressions in generation outputs (smoke eval corpus)
Feature guarded behind runtime flag and rollout A/B with clear metrics in the Console
tasks: Design: formalize entropy metric and bucket merge/split heuristics
Implementation: ingress bucketer + lightweight histogram producer
Implementation: pad-shearing transformation and compact KV allocator
Implementation: kernel-hint interface and scheduler integration
Integration test: microbench harness for fused vs unfused kernels per-bucket
Staging: A/B test on 3 representative routes, capture pad/token and tail-latency
Docs: console dashboard tile + rollout runbook
Perf: tune bucket thresholds and backpressure to meet latency SLOs
design_notes:
High-level approach: compute a 1D summary per request (sequence_length, prefix_hash, estimated_entropy) at ingress. Maintain a short-lived bucket table keyed by quantized length + entropy band. Buckets self-tessellate: when intra-bucket variance exceeds threshold we split; when two neighbor buckets show similar kernel preferences and low combined variance we merge. Entropy used to avoid grouping bursty sequences (chat-style with variable lengths) with deterministic prompt-heavy sequences. Pad-shearing removes trailing padding words by compacting sequences and storing per-item alignment metadata so subsequent KV cache accesses map to compact offsets. This enables contiguous GPU memory layouts and reduced memcpy during prefill. Kernel hinting: emit a three-bit hint (FUSED_FAST | FUSED_SMALLSPAN | FALLBACK) per bucket for the runtime optimizer to choose attention kernel variant.

Memory model: pad-shearing uses a per-batch offset table stored in pinned host memory to minimize device-bound bookkeeping. We allocate compacted KV buffers per bucket and maintain a lightweight mapping to original request IDs for re-expansion at response time. Trade-offs: extra bookkeeping increases CPU overhead at very high QPS; mitigate by sampling heavy routes and falling back to legacy coalescer under CPU pressure.
tradeoffs:
- Pro: Significant pad reduction and improved kernel utilization for common bucket sizes.
- Con: Added complexity in request bookkeeping and potential CPU overhead at extreme QPS.
- Pro: Kernel hints allow runtime to pick high-throughput kernels for common lengths.
- Con: Some model variants (sparse attention or operator-incompatible kernels) will need to fall back, adding fragmentation.
- Decision: start conservative (merge thresholds high, enable pad-shearing only for buckets >16 tokens) and iterate based on staging metrics.
performance_targets: Baseline: current coalescer at median padding ratio 38% (padded tokens / total tokens) on target routes. Target: reduce to <=30% median and <=25% for top-10 routes. Kernel hinting target: end-to-end tokens/sec improvement >=8% on affected buckets in microbench. Latency SLO: p99 increase <=5%.
measurement_plan:
- Instrumentation: per-bucket pad_token_count, bucket_variance, kernel_hint_chosen, prefill_coalesced_count.
- Dashboards: new 'Tessellator' Console page with per-route pad reduction heatmap and tail-latency comparison.
- A/B: enable feature for 10% of traffic on staging when microbench targets met; collect 72h windows.
- Regression tests: smoke eval set for correctness, plus token-level diff checks for determinism-sensitive routes.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature gated behind runtime-flag; 2) Canary: 1% traffic with conservative buckets; 3) Stage: 10% for 48-72h; 4) Ramp to 50% if pad reduction observed and latency stable; 5) Full rollout after 7 days of stable metrics. Automatic fallback if CPU load > preset threshold or p99 exceeds allowed delta.
qa_checks: Run smoke evals (generation) across 5 model families and ensure token diffs within noise band
Verify pad token metrics surfaced in Console for canary cohort
Load test: 2x peak QPS workload with tessellator enabled and confirm no OOM/GC thrashing

risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: CPU overhead causing degraded p95/p99 under high QPS. Mitigation: adaptive sampling (enable tessellator only for heavy routes with >X tokens/sec), fall back to legacy coalescer when node CPU > threshold.

Risk: Kernel fragmentation causing many small buckets to pick fallback kernels. Mitigation: merge heuristic tuned to prefer kernel-uniformity across adjacent length bands. Add telemetry to measure 'kernel fragmentation' and auto-merge buckets based on cost model.
next_steps: 1) Complete PR reviews and land proto bucketer behind flag. 2) Add host-side zeroization for offset tables per security review. 3) Run 72h staging A/B and collect pad and latency metrics. 4) Iterate bucket split/merge thresholds based on staging results.
